display.title: Dayeinu: The Old Man, the King's Lost Ring and the Pesach Seder
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Pesach story told by a grandmother: an old man who always provided Pesach for the poor promises to find the king's lost ring, and the singing of 'Dayeinu' at his Seder reveals the thief.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish by a grandmother to her grandchildren. An old man who used to give four hundred poor families everything they needed for Pesach has lost all his money, and Pesach is coming. He is a trusted adviser to the king, and often talks him out of harsh decrees urged by a wicked minister named Yena, who hates the Jews. When the king takes off his precious coronation ring to wash, Yena pockets it. The king offers fifty thousand dollars to whoever finds it. Trusting in Hashem, the old man asks the king for twenty-five thousand in advance, promising to find the ring with Hashem's help, and uses it to clothe and feed the poor for Yom Tov. The king's detectives think the crowds of poor people are searching for the ring. On Seder night the king and queen come in disguise to the old man's window and hear everyone singing 'Dayeinu', which sounds like 'Di Yena!' The king rushes to the minister's house and gets his ring back, and the old man thanks Hashem for helping him because he helped the poor.
display.lesson: Help the poor generously and trust Hashem; He repays those who care for others.

advisories.note: A wicked minister urges the king to make harsh decrees against the Jews; the old man fears jail if he fails.
The old man has lost everything and sold his furniture and his wife's clothes.
